'''Sharon C. Glotzer''' is an American scientist and "digital [[alchemist]]",<ref>{{cite web|title='Digital Alchemist' Seeks Rules of Emergence|date=8 March 2017|url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/digital-alchemist-sharon-glotzer-seeks-rules-of-emergence-20170308/|publisher=Quanta Magazine|access-date=23 October 2018}}</ref> the [[John W. Cahn|John Werner Cahn]] Distinguished University Professor of Engineering and the [[Stuart W. Churchill]] Collegiate Professor of Chemical Engineering at the [[University of Michigan]], where she is also professor of materials science and engineering, professor of physics, professor of macromolecular science and engineering, and professor of applied physics. From 2017-2025, she served as the Anthony C. Lembke Department Chair of Chemical Engineering at Michigan. She is recognized  for her contributions to the fields of [[soft matter]] and computational science, most notably on problems in assembly science and engineering, nanoscience, and the [[glass transition]], for which the elucidation of the nature of  [[dynamical heterogeneity]] in glassy liquids is of particular significance. She is a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]], the [[National Academy of Engineering]], and the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]. In 2023 she was named a [[List of Clarivate Citation laureates in Physics|Clarivate Citation Laureate in Physics]], joining a cohort of 23 world-class researchers who have made significant contributions across a diverse range of fields. Her scientific publications have been cited more than 40,000 times, and she has an h-index of 98 (Google Scholar 11/24/25).

==Education==
Glotzer obtained her [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] in physics at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]], in 1987, and her PhD in 1993 in theoretical soft [[condensed matter]] physics research under the guidance of [[H. Eugene Stanley]] at [[Boston University]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Sharon C. Glotzer - Chemical Engineering|url=http://che.engin.umich.edu/people/glotzer.html#+section_1|publisher=College of Engineering, University of Michigan|access-date=9 February 2013|archive-date=11 June 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100611090629/http://che.engin.umich.edu/people/glotzer.html#+section_1|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Academic career==
Sharon Glotzer joined the National Institute of Standards and Technology [[NIST]] in Gaithersburg, Maryland, in 1993 as a National Research Council postdoctoral fellow in the Polymers Division of the Materials Science & Engineering Laboratory. She became a permanent member of the Polymers Division, and was the co-founder, deputy director, and then director of the [[NIST]] Center for Theoretical and Computational Materials Science from 1994 to 2000. In January 2001 she moved to the [[University of Michigan]] as a tenured associate professor in Chemical Engineering and in Materials Science & Engineering. She is now the [[John W. Cahn|John Werner Cahn]] Distinguished University Professor of Engineering and the Stuart W. Churchill Collegiate Professor of Chemical Engineering. From 2017 to 2025 she served as the Anthony C. Lembke Department Chair of Chemical Engineering. Glotzer holds additional appointments in Materials Science and Engineering, Physics, Applied Physics, and Macromolecular Science and Engineering, and is a core member of the Biointerfaces Institute. She has served on numerous boards, including the Division of Physical Sciences Board and the Chemical Sciences and Technology Board of the [[National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine]]. She served as associate editor of the leading nanoscience journal ''[[ACS Nano]]'' from 2014 to 2024, and is now an associate editor of ''JACS'', the ''[[Journal of the American Chemical Society]]''.

==Research and achievements==
Glotzer made fundamental contributions to the field of the [[glass transition]], for which the [[molecular dynamics]] simulation of [[Lennard-Jones potential|Lennard-Jones]] particles exhibiting dynamical heterogeneity in the form of string-like motion in a 3D-liquid<ref>{{cite journal |title=Dynamical Heterogeneities in a Supercooled Lennard-Jones Liquid |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=79 |issue=15 |pages=2827–2830 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.79.2827 |year=1997 |last1=Kob |first1=Walter |last2=Donati |first2=Claudio |last3=Plimpton |first3=Steven J. |last4=Poole |first4=Peter H. |last5=Glotzer |first5=Sharon C. |arxiv=cond-mat/9706075 |bibcode=1997PhRvL..79.2827K |s2cid=14823693 }}</ref> is of particular significance.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Heterogeneity at the glass transition: a review | doi = 10.1016/S0022-3093(98)00831-X |bibcode=1999JNCS..243...81S |volume=243 |issue=2–3 |journal=Journal of Non-Crystalline Solids |pages=81–108|year=1999 |last1=Sillescu |first1=Hans }}</ref> In addition, her paper together with [[Michael J. Solomon]] on anisotropy dimensions of patchy particles<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Glotzer SC |author2=Solomon MJ | year = 2007| title =  Anisotropy of building blocks and their assembly into complex structures| journal = Nature Materials | volume = 6 | issue = 8| pages = 557–562 | doi=10.1038/nmat1949|pmid=17667968 |bibcode=2007NatMa...6..557G }}</ref> has become a classic work, inspiring research directions of groups around the world. Glotzer and collaborators also hold the record for the densest [[tetrahedron packing]] and discovered that hard [[tetrahedron]]s can self-assemble into a dodecagonal [[quasicrystal]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Haji-Akbari | first1=Amir | last2=Engel | first2=Michael | last3=Keys | first3=Aaron S. | last4=Zheng | first4=Xiaoyu | last5=Petschek | first5=Rolfe G. | last6=Palffy-Muhoray | first6=Peter | last7=Glotzer | first7=Sharon C. | title=Disordered, quasicrystalline and crystalline phases of densely packed tetrahedra | journal=Nature | volume=462 | issue=7274 | pages=773–777 | year=2009 | pmid=20010683 | doi=10.1038/nature08641 | bibcode=2009Natur.462..773H|arxiv = 1012.5138 | s2cid=4412674 }}</ref>

Glotzer and collaborators coined the term ‘Directional Entropic Forces’<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1021/nn204012y |pmid=22098586 |title=Crystalline Assemblies and Densest Packings of a Family of Truncated Tetrahedra and the Role of Directional Entropic Forces |journal=ACS Nano |volume=6 |issue=1 |pages=609–14 |arxiv=1109.1323|year=2012 |last1=Damasceno |first1=Pablo F. |last2=Engel |first2=Michael |last3=Glotzer |first3=Sharon C. |bibcode=2012ACSNa...6..609D |s2cid=12785227 }}</ref> in 2011 to denote the effective interaction that drives anisotropic hard particles to align their facets during self-assembly and/or crystallization. This idea, which builds on [[Lars Onsager|Onsager]]'s work on spherocylinders,<ref>{{cite journal |doi= 10.1111/j.1749-6632.1949.tb27296.x|title= The Effects of Shape on the Interaction of Colloidal Particles|journal= Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences|volume= 51|issue= 4|pages= 627–659|year= 1949|last1= Onsager|first1= Lars|bibcode= 1949NYASA..51..627O|s2cid= 84562683}}</ref> allows for predictions of expected assembled crystal and crystal-like structures from attributes of the particles' shape.<ref>{{cite arXiv |eprint=1202.2177|title=Structural Diversity and the Role of Particle Shape and Dense Fluid Behavior in Assemblies of Hard Polyhedra |last1= Damasceno |first1=Pablo F. |last2=Engel |first2=Michael |last3= Glotzer |first3=Sharon C. |class=cond-mat.soft |year=2012 }}</ref>

Glotzer has served as PhD advisor to 85 graduate students, and mentored 30 postdoctoral and senior researchers in her group. She has published 343 peer-reviewed scientific papers. According to Google Scholar, her publications have received over 44,200 citations and her [[h-index]] is 98.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=H_YM2p8AAAAJ&hl=en |title=Google Scholar: Sharon Glotzer |access-date=24 November 2025 }}</ref>

==Honors and awards==
Glotzer was elected to the [[National Academy of Engineering]] in 2019 for the development of computer-based design principles for assembly engineering and manufacturing of advanced materials and nanotechnology.<ref>{{cite web|title=National Academy of Engineering Elects 86 Members and 18 Foreign Members |url=https://www.nae.edu/204037.aspx|publisher=National Academy of Engineering|access-date=11 February 2019}}</ref> She was also elected a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2014 and the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2011. She is a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]], the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]], the [[American Institute of Chemical Engineers]], and the [[Materials Research Society]]. She is a member of the second inaugural class of [[United States Department of Defense|Department of Defense]] {{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20121212014704/http://www.defense.gov/releases/release.aspx?releaseid=13267|title=National Security Science and Engineering (now Vannevar Bush) Faculty Fellows}}, and received the award again in 2022, and she was named a [[Simons Foundation#Simons Investigators awardees|Simons Investigator]]<ref>[https://simonsfoundation.org/mps-funded-programs-simons-investigators Simons' Investigator], simonsfoundation.org</ref> in 2012, part of the inaugural class of Investigators. Like the MacArthur "Genius" Awardees, both Vannevar Bush Faculty Fellows and Simons Investigators receive significant funding to pursue unrestricted basic research. Glotzer is the recipient of numerous awards, including the Nanoscale Science & Engineering Forum Award, the [[Alpha Chi Sigma]] Award and the Charles M.A. Stine (now Braskem) Award, all from the [[American Institute of Chemical Engineers]] (AIChE); the Turnbull Lectureship Award and the MRS Medal, both from the [[Materials Research Society]]; the Irving Langmuir Award for Chemical Physics, the Aneesur Rahman Prize in Computational Physics and the [[Maria Goeppert-Mayer Award]], all from the [[American Physical Society]]; the FOMMS Medal for Foundations in Molecular & Materials Simulation; a Presidential Early Career Award for Scientists and Engineers (PECASE); and a Department of Commerce Bronze Medal Award for Superior Federal Service. In 2014, she became an associate editor of ''[[ACS Nano]]''.,<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1021/acsnano.5b01418 |pmid=25802086 |title=Nanoscience ''vs'' Nanotechnology—Defining the Field |journal=ACS Nano |volume=9 |issue=3 |pages=2215–7 |year=2015 |last1=Mulvaney |first1=Paul |bibcode=2015ACSNa...9.2215M |doi-access=free }}</ref> where she served until 2024. She is now Associate Editor of JACS.
